tools.name: start_meeting
tools.description: Starts a new Meetful video meeting and returns its link. The link opens in any browser with no account and no download. Meetful can email the link to up to 10 addresses.

tools.name: invite
tools.description: Emails the link to a running meeting to up to 10 people, from the signed-in person's name, and returns a message with the link.

tools.name: list_meetings
tools.description: Lists the signed-in person's meetings that are still running, with how many people are in each.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Returns the full transcript of a meeting with the speaker on every line. Each microphone is transcribed on its own, so the name on a line is the person whose microphone it came from.

tools.name: get_notes
tools.description: Returns what the room has drawn from the conversation so far: decisions, open questions, actions and disagreements, each with a verbatim quote from the transcript. Items that fail that check are marked unverified.

tools.name: get_action_items
tools.description: Returns the verified commitments from one finished recording the signed-in person owns: each action, its owner, its status and a link to the line it came from.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Posts a message in a meeting's chat under the agent's own name. Everyone in the call sees it.

tools.name: list_recordings
tools.description: Lists the signed-in person's recordings and clips, newest first, with their links, optionally for one meeting. Each link opens for whoever that recording's sharing setting allows.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Files feedback about Meetful (a bug, a confusing moment or an idea) on the list the product is built from, and returns a link to follow it. With fix set, it becomes a fix request that a person reviews before anything changes.

tools.name: submit_fix
tools.description: Opens a pull request against Meetful's source code: a unified diff for a fix request, either an existing one (feedback_id) or a new one described in text. Nothing is applied automatically; a person reviews and merges it.

tools.name: import_transcript
tools.description: Imports a meeting transcript or chat log from another tool into the signed-in person's Meetful dashboard: .vtt or .srt captions, plain-text transcripts, Read AI JSON, JSON lists of turns, Google Meet and Zoom chat logs, or a WhatsApp export. Speaker labels are kept as written. Returns the new meetin

tools.name: send_notetaker
tools.description: Sends the Meetful notetaker to a Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex meeting. It joins as a participant and records; when the call ends, the transcript, recap and action items appear in the signed-in person's dashboard. Requires signing in; usage is counted in minutes per month by plan.

tools.name: my_tasks
tools.description: Lists the tasks handed to the signed-in person from their calls: who asked, what they asked for, which call, and the status of each. Open tasks come first.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Returns one task handed over from a call in full: the request in the asker's words, who asked, the lines of the call just before it, and any Meetful fix request it concerns.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Sets a task's status (working, done or blocked) with a short note and links. The call the task came from sees the update in its chat.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.description: Joins a Meetful call the signed-in person is in or started, as their agent. The agent appears in the call under the person's name, is announced in the chat, and anyone in the call can remove it.

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Returns what happens next in a call the agent has joined: new transcript lines with their speakers, new chat messages and tasks handed to the agent. It returns as soon as something new arrives, or after wait_seconds, with a "next" value marking where it stopped. An agent that has not read for 90 sec

tools.name: hand_off
tools.description: Hands a task to another participant's agent in the current call. The task appears in the call for that person to accept.

tools.name: set_up_booking_page
tools.description: Creates a Meetful booking page (meetful.com/<handle>) and returns the code to put it on a website: a one-line button, the page inline, an iframe, or a plain link. Every booking gets its own video room. For a signed-in person the page is theirs and live at once; otherwise the result includes a claim

tools.name: booking_page_status
tools.description: Reports whether a booking page is live (claimed by its owner), still waiting, or gone, with the code to embed it.

tools.name: find_times
tools.description: Lists open times on someone's Meetful booking link (meetful.com/<name>), as exact UTC instants and in the owner's time zone, with the meeting lengths and any questions the page asks. No sign-in needed.

tools.name: book_time
tools.description: Books a time on someone's Meetful booking link for the person using the assistant. Returns the meeting link, a calendar file and a private link to move or cancel; the owner is told an assistant made the booking. If the time was taken meanwhile, the error lists the nearest open times. No sign-in need

tools.name: get_my_context
tools.description: Returns the signed-in person's profile as Meetful holds it, in the Protext format (protext.org): name, verified email, booking link, time zone and recent meetings, each with its source.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_transcript, get_notes, send_feedback, import_transcript, listen, get_my_context · Private data: send_feedback, send_notetaker, book_time · Public sink: start_meeting, send_message, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, get_my_context · Destructive: join_meeting, get_my_context.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_transcript, get_notes, send_feedback, import_transcript, listen, get_my_context · Private data: send_feedback, send_notetaker, book_time · Public sink: start_meeting, send_message, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, get_my_context · Destructive: join_meeting, get_my_context

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
